answer: Each identity must seal a private sector: the epoch corpus encrypted under a per-identity key, cut into a dune of fixed grains and committed as a Merkle root in its answer. Peers hold a lantern on random grain runs and demand retrieval within a short window, so the bytes must stay hot. Two keys posting one root are a mirror of a single storehouse; a deduped copy stalls once the drawn range is the replica the farm dropped. The cost is per identity and non-poolable, distinct sealed bytes plus a live window, so fifty clones cannot share one drive. Skip the seal and one audit exposes the copy.
